name: Jefferson River (Twin Bridges)
blurb: Upper Jefferson floats around Twin Bridges and Whitehall, with quiet trout water, braided channels and access at FWP fishing sites. Check irrigation diversions and low-water conditions.

sections.notes: Short upper-river float. Check the launch-side diversion before starting; the estimate excludes scouting and carrying.

notices.title: Hell’s Canyon launch approach
notices.text: The launch sits behind an island with a diversion downstream. The trail guide describes paddling upstream from the launch to reach the main channel. Scout this connection before starting.

sections.routeReview: The partial dotted course starts below the launch/diversion area. Exact landing connections and passage around the diversion are not mapped. Banks, bars and side channels can differ from this approximate overview.

putInAccess.note: Public boating access and ramp type are documented by FWP. This marker locates the access area; it is not a verified water-edge ramp pin.
putInAccess.directions: About 3 miles south of Silver Star, then 0.5 mile upstream of the bridge on the county road. The launch is behind an island; the canoe-trail guide describes returning upstream to reach the main river and avoiding the diversion downstream of the island.

takeOutAccess.note: FWP documents the fishing-access site and concrete ramp. Satellite comparison shows the agency coordinate set back from the channel, so it is displayed as an access area rather than an exact water-edge landing.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the signed Silver Star FWP fishing access beside the Jefferson River crossing. FWP documents a concrete ramp; this agency coordinate locates the facility, so confirm the exact ramp at the site.

sections.notes: Planning estimate for time on the water only. Add time for scouting, carrying and any portage. Confirm the exact landing and local conditions before setting your shuttle.

notices.title: Waterloo / Parsons diversion dam
notices.text: Waterloo has a diversion beside the road access. The canoe-trail organization documents a ramp and public portage. Scout the exact landing, launch and portage before floating; this area marker does not show a safe passage through the dam.

takeOutAccess.note: FWP documents the public site and facility coordinates, with difficult access and no listed boat facilities. Preserve this as an approximate area, not an exact landing, ramp or bank-side claim.
takeOutAccess.directions: Follow Parrot Castle Road to Daly Road and the parking area described by FWP. Access to the river is difficult and involves a slough. Confirm a suitable landing for your craft.

notices.title: Braided channels and low water
notices.text: The canoe-trail guide describes several channels below Kountz Bridge and low-water limitations. Channel depth changes; check conditions before launching.

sections.routeReview: Access areas remain available. The source course crosses shifted banks and bars, and its roughly 3.4-mile length differs from the 5-mile published planning distance. Channel choice and exact landing connections remain under review.

putInAccess.note: Public boating access and ramp type are documented by FWP. This marker locates the access area; it is not a verified water-edge ramp pin.
putInAccess.directions: From Whitehall, follow Kountz Road about 6 miles southwest to the fishing access site. FWP documents a concrete ramp and vault toilet; confirm the ramp and current channel at the site.

takeOutAccess.note: Public boating access and ramp type are documented by FWP. This marker locates the access area; it is not a verified water-edge ramp pin.
takeOutAccess.directions: From Whitehall, take Highway 2 about 4 miles east, then Mayflower Road about 3 miles south. FWP documents a concrete ramp; confirm the exact landing at the bridge before arranging the shuttle.

sections.notes: Short valley float ending at Cardwell before the canyon. Use the published guide distance for planning; the upstream gauge does not measure every diversion.
